值得閱讀的理由

  • 從永和槍擊案切入，呈現一場突發暴力事件如何震撼選舉現場，並牽動全台政治氣氛。
  • 梳理馬英九政府上任後的經濟與災害應對考驗，說明藍綠勢力如何在選前消長。
  • 解析五都改制、候選人布局與政治人物的總統大位考量，帶出選戰背後的策略角力。
  • 回顧郝龍斌市政爭議與蘇貞昌、蔡英文的選擇，理解2010年台北市長選戰的形成脈絡。

摘要

永和槍響：選前夜的震撼

2010年11月26日，五都選舉前夕，台北縣永和市的造勢活動傳出槍聲。站在台上為議員候選人陳鴻源助選的連勝文臉部中彈，子彈也波及一名民眾，對方不幸身亡。連勝文緊急送醫，經台大醫院醫療團隊搶救後脫離險境，並逐漸康復。檢方調查認定，槍手原本意圖刺殺陳鴻源，因兩人臨時更換位置，連勝文才意外成為目標。槍擊讓選舉造勢瞬間轉為悲憤，也使台灣社會再度陷入政治暴力與未知恐慌的陰影。

政局轉折與五都改制

作者將時間帶回2008年，馬英九以高票當選總統，國民黨也在立法院占有優勢，藍營一度氣勢如虹。然而，金融海嘯重創經濟，股市大幅下跌；2009年莫拉克風災後，政府的救災表現又遭到批評，馬政府聲望下滑。民進黨則在蔡英文帶領下，逐步走出2008年敗選低潮，並在地方選舉與立委補選中回升。

2010年，台灣進行五都改制，台北縣升格為新北市，台中、台南與高雄則改制或合併為直轄市，地方選舉也因此延後舉行。改制帶來行政資源與席次變化，也引發各種政治揣測，並加劇民進黨內部的提名競爭。無論改制背後是否另有盤算，民進黨的重要人物都必須投入五都選戰。

台北市的市政挑戰與選戰布局

國民黨已在台北市執政多年，但郝龍斌第一任期面臨不少市政風波。貓空纜車因颱風造成塔柱地基問題而停駛一年半；內湖線通車後故障頻繁，甚至發生乘客受困高架軌道的狀況，遭網友譏稱「爆炸彎」。這些事件使郝龍斌支持度跌落，也讓民進黨看見重奪台北市的機會。

民進黨原先盤算由蔡英文角逐台北市長、蘇貞昌參選新北市長，認為這樣較有勝算。但蘇貞昌與蔡英文都被視為2012年總統大選的潛在人選，參選五都時也面臨政治進退的盤算：若當選市長，日後角逐總統可能被視為離職另謀高就；若在台北敗選，則有機會轉而投入總統選戰。

蘇貞昌改變布局，北台灣對決成形

2010年3月，蘇貞昌在保安宮前宣布參選台北市長，並承諾若當選便做滿任期、不考慮參選2012年總統。他還以美國總統華盛頓為例，強調民主政治應抵抗權力誘惑。蘇的宣布打亂黨中央原先的安排，蔡英文隨後轉而投入新北市長選戰。於是，台北市形成郝龍斌對決蘇貞昌的局面，新北市則由蔡英文迎戰朱立倫，北台灣兩座城市成為全台選戰焦點。

從年初的市政爭議到選前夜的致命槍響，2010年的台北市長選戰籠罩在政治競逐與社會不安之中。永和槍擊案不只改變了造勢現場的氣氛，也使這場五都選舉增添難以預料的陰影；作者由此展開對歷屆台北市長選舉的回顧。

  • 梳理馬英九政府上任後的經濟與災害應對考驗，說明藍綠勢力如何在選前消長。
  • 解析五都改制、候選人布局與政治人物的總統大位考量，帶出選戰背後的策略角力。
  • 回顧郝龍斌市政爭議與蘇貞昌、蔡英文的選擇，理解2010年台北市長選戰的形成脈絡。

摘要

永和槍響：選前夜的震撼

2010年11月26日，五都選舉前夕，台北縣永和市的造勢活動傳出槍聲。站在台上為議員候選人陳鴻源助選的連勝文臉部中彈，子彈也波及一名民眾，對方不幸身亡。連勝文緊急送醫，經台大醫院醫療團隊搶救後脫離險境，並逐漸康復。檢方調查認定，槍手原本意圖刺殺陳鴻源，因兩人臨時更換位置，連勝文才意外成為目標。槍擊讓選舉造勢瞬間轉為悲憤，也使台灣社會再度陷入政治暴力與未知恐慌的陰影。

政局轉折與五都改制

作者將時間帶回2008年，馬英九以高票當選總統，國民黨也在立法院占有優勢，藍營一度氣勢如虹。然而，金融海嘯重創經濟，股市大幅下跌；2009年莫拉克風災後，政府的救災表現又遭到批評，馬政府聲望下滑。民進黨則在蔡英文帶領下，逐步走出2008年敗選低潮，並在地方選舉與立委補選中回升。

2010年，台灣進行五都改制，台北縣升格為新北市，台中、台南與高雄則改制或合併為直轄市，地方選舉也因此延後舉行。改制帶來行政資源與席次變化，也引發各種政治揣測，並加劇民進黨內部的提名競爭。無論改制背後是否另有盤算，民進黨的重要人物都必須投入五都選戰。

台北市的市政挑戰與選戰布局

國民黨已在台北市執政多年，但郝龍斌第一任期面臨不少市政風波。貓空纜車因颱風造成塔柱地基問題而停駛一年半；內湖線通車後故障頻繁，甚至發生乘客受困高架軌道的狀況，遭網友譏稱「爆炸彎」。這些事件使郝龍斌支持度跌落，也讓民進黨看見重奪台北市的機會。

民進黨原先盤算由蔡英文角逐台北市長、蘇貞昌參選新北市長，認為這樣較有勝算。但蘇貞昌與蔡英文都被視為2012年總統大選的潛在人選，參選五都時也面臨政治進退的盤算：若當選市長，日後角逐總統可能被視為離職另謀高就；若在台北敗選，則有機會轉而投入總統選戰。

蘇貞昌改變布局，北台灣對決成形

2010年3月，蘇貞昌在保安宮前宣布參選台北市長，並承諾若當選便做滿任期、不考慮參選2012年總統。他還以美國總統華盛頓為例，強調民主政治應抵抗權力誘惑。蘇的宣布打亂黨中央原先的安排，蔡英文隨後轉而投入新北市長選戰。於是，台北市形成郝龍斌對決蘇貞昌的局面，新北市則由蔡英文迎戰朱立倫，北台灣兩座城市成為全台選戰焦點。

從年初的市政爭議到選前夜的致命槍響，2010年的台北市長選戰籠罩在政治競逐與社會不安之中。永和槍擊案不只改變了造勢現場的氣氛，也使這場五都選舉增添難以預料的陰影；作者由此展開對歷屆台北市長選舉的回顧。

While past campaigns would. release one or two theme songs, Su’s. team produced a full urban concept. album, "Open Taipei," featuring 11. tracks, 20 creative teams, and 33. musicians, with songs in Mandarin,. Taiwanese, Hakka, English, and even.

Vietnamese. Because many singers were. tied to management contracts, they had. to appear under pseudonyms, such as " Shui Xi Gong." Fire EX. became "P-Li. Bird No. 4," Suming became "San Yin," and PTT music critics even called it. one of the best Mandarin albums of 2010. . Su’s campaign headquarters was. named the "Beyond Shop," a concept. store selling cultural goods, hosting. lectures, and playing music; young. people could drink coffee inside and. take home campaign merchandise at the. same time. To connect the campaign with. the rising online communities of that. time, Su hired a video team to film the. campaign staff’s daily routines,. launching an "Open Campaign" reality. show, updated weekly on YouTube. However, the stars of the videos. weren't the candidates, but Su’s. staffers. Through their perspective,. the public not only understood the. practical operations of a campaign but. also got closer to Su Tseng-chang as a. person—a first in Taiwan's election. history. This set of propaganda and. visual systems can be said to have. completely overturned election. aesthetics. To tell a story from 10. years later: in January 2021, when the. Control Yuan released its financial. disclosure report, Su Tseng-chang, then. Premier, declared a collection of items. worth zero dollars, including designs. for "Open Taipei,""Beyond Taipei," and. the "Beyond Shop." These were all from. his 2010 campaign. He clearly still. views the design of that visual system. as a priceless asset even today. As for. Hau Lung-bin, the KMT Central Committee. officially nominated him for. re-election in May. He immediately set. his campaign theme as "Taipei Fly High,. " appealing to the timing of his. governance, with KMT Secretary-General. King Pu-tsung directing the campaign,. hoping to reawaken the dense grassroots. base of the Blue camp in Taipei and. replicate the winning script of the. past few years. Throughout the first. half of the year, various polls were. neck-and-neck within the margin of. error. According to a TVBS poll in May,. Hau Lung-bin had 46%and Su Tseng-chang. had 41%. Hau led by a small margin most. of the time, but the lead never widened. enough to make the Blue camp feel. secure. It was right at this moment. that an unforeseen storm erupted,. triggered by nothing but a single stalk. . In 2010, the Taipei City Government. was busy from top to bottom preparing. for the Taipei International Flora. Exposition, or "Flora Expo" for short. Mayor Hau Lung-bin positioned the Flora. Expo as a major international event,. pouring massive funding and resources. into preparations and promotion. The. lineup of celebrity spokespersons was. incredibly luxurious, from image. ambassador Lin Chi-ling to theme song. performers like S.H.E., Jay Chou, A-Mei. , and Mayday—all were spokespeople. for the Expo. Since it was a. world-class expo, opposition city. councilors immediately grabbed their. magnifying glasses to scrutinize it. They didn't know what they would find,. but they were shocked by what they saw. This investigation uncovered the most. famous batch of vegetables in Taiwan's. electoral history. A single stalk of. water spinach planted in the Flora Expo. park was priced at 500 NTD, meaning one. stalk cost 20 NTD. Other items like. basil and bok choy—things that cost. just a few dozen dollars at the market. —all appeared on the list with. absurdly high unit prices. Think about. it: the general public might not. understand urban planning budget items,. but everyone knows what 500 NTD for. water spinach means—every mom who has. been to a wet market understands that. perfectly. This controversy immediately. escalated into a political crisis for. Hau Lung-bin. Political talk shows. discussed every night why a single. stalk of water spinach could skyrocket. to over a hundred dollars. Opposition. councilors even went directly to the.

Taipei District Prosecutors Office to. sue Hau for corruption and cronyism. As. soon as the water spinach scandal broke. , the city government punished two. officials from the Parks and Street. Lights Office and referred the. consulting firm for investigation,. emphasizing that there was no. corruption, only an issue with the. vendor's quoting and pricing units. The. Blue camp hit back, saying the. opposition was using a magnifying glass. to find faults and slapping a. corruption label on the Flora Expo. They emphasized that the Expo lasted. for six months and the plants had to be. replaced several times, so the unit. prices naturally couldn't be compared. to a wet market. However, the more the. city government tried to explain, the. worse it got! Spokesperson Chao. Hsin-ping emphasized that the. specifications for the water spinach at. the Flora Expo were different from what. people buy at the market: they were 20. centimeters by 20 centimeters. But this. explanation failed to clarify that it. was the planting area, and it. immediately became a laughingstock. People joked, "Where on earth could you. grow such thick water spinach?" Facing. the political crisis sparked by Hau. Lung-bin over the water spinach scandal. , Su Tseng-chang’s camp played it. smart, continuing to host town hall. meetings and concerts to discuss their. vision for the city. As for the polls,. the tide turned; the September 8th TVBS. poll showed Su Tseng-chang leading Hau. Lung-bin 42%to 39%. TVBS also projected. the final vote share. If the election. were held tomorrow, Su Tseng-chang. would receive 52%and Hau Lung-bin 48%. In other words, with less than three. months to go, the incumbent mayor was. trailing in major media polls, and. internal KMT rumors began to spread. that the Flora Expo would drag down the. five-city elections. Beyond that,. prosecutors began investigating the. Xinsheng Elevated Bridge renovation. project, meaning Hau Lung-bin was. facing not just a propaganda war, but. an administrative one. On the evening. of September 13, 2010, the Taipei City. Government held an emergency press. conference where Hau Lung-bin. personally stepped in front of the. cameras to announce the resignation of. Deputy Mayor Lee Yong-ping. Mayor's. advisor Chuang Wen-szu and Mayor's. chief secretary Jen Hsiao-chi also had. their resignations approved. These. three were all core staff members of. the city government. Outsiders. interpreted it bluntly: this was a " tail-cutting to survive" tactic to. salvage a dismal campaign. Of course,. firing people wasn't enough; Hau. Lung-bin also publicly apologized to. the citizens, admitted to procurement. mismanagement, and released the entire. Flora Expo procurement list for public. scrutiny. The goal, naturally, was to. ensure the Flora Expo, set to begin. trial operations in October, could. distance itself from the cloud of. scandal. In truth, at this stage of the. battle, both Blue and Green camps had. exhausted their ammunition of scandals. and attacks. Only one thing remained to. decide the outcome: was the Flora Expo. actually any good? After all, with 9.5. billion NTD invested and the label of. an "international event," if it. accidentally became an international. laughingstock, Hau Lung-bin—who hoped. the Expo would boost his campaign—. might find his poll numbers sinking. even further. As the Flora Expo began. its trial runs in October, the four. major park areas showcased the full. integration of Taiwan’s unique floral. technology and innovation. The first. citizens to enter emerged and told. reporters, "It’s really beautiful. Waiting in line for so long was worth. it." By the time of the official. opening on November 6, the massive. crowds immediately captured media. attention. The positive publicity. quickly overshadowed the previous wave.

of negativity. Television news. headlines shifted from "500 NTD for a. head of water spinach" to "Dream. Pavilion reservation tickets sold out. in seconds." With floral displays and. fireworks, the Flora Expo transformed. from Hau Lung-pin's biggest burden into. his greatest asset for reelection. Forty days after opening, the number of. visitors surpassed two million, and. visitor satisfaction reached a high of. eighty percent; Hau Lung-pin's poll. numbers rebounded along with it. In the. final TVBS poll before the election,. Hau stood at 49%and Su Tseng-chang at. 39%, with the gap widening back to 10. percentage points. However, because Su. Tseng-chang had led in the polls for a. period, the Pan-Green camp remained. optimistic. As for the Pan-Blue side,. despite seeing polls that showed a lead. , they still wouldn't guarantee a. victory. The race remained in this. state of anxious tension. Thus. We. return to the opening night, November. 26, 2010, the eve of the five-city. elections. Hau Lung-pin held a rally on. Ketagalan Boulevard, while Su. Tseng-chang hosted a concert-style. event at the Huashan Creative Park,. hoping to keep the joyful, positive. election atmosphere going until the. very last moment. Yet, the happy. atmosphere took a sharp turn for the. worse. At 8:00 PM, over at Yonghe. Elementary School, city councilor Chen. Hung-yuan was holding his pre-election. rally, having invited Sean Lien, a. member of the KMT Central Committee, to. speak on stage. At 8:17 PM, a man in. black climbed onto the stage, grabbed. Sean Lien around the neck from behind,. pulled out a handgun, and fired a shot. at his face at close range, with the. bullet passing through his left cheek. and exiting near his right temple. Unexpectedly, one shot wasn't enough; he tried to fire a second! At that. moment, the handgun jammed, and those. on stage rushed forward to subdue him. This man was named Lin Cheng-wei, 48. years old, a local gang member from. Yonghe nicknamed "Horse Face." The. bullet that passed through Sean Lien's. face flew into the crowd below,. striking a 29-year-old man in a. wheelchair named Huang Yun-sheng. He. was rushed to Gengxin Hospital, but. attempts to save him failed. He was the. one who truly lost his life that night. As for Sean Lien, covered in blood, he. was first sent to Yonghe Gengxin. Hospital, then transferred to National. Taiwan University Hospital, where he. survived after emergency surgery. When. the news reached the Ketagalan. Boulevard rally, Hau Lung-pin's event. was underway. The crowd was instantly. incensed, especially when Sean Lien's. father, Lien Chan, stepped onto Hau's. stage. The audience and those on stage. were instantly reduced to tears, and. Lien Chan said this:. >> I support Hau Lung-bin to be elected by. a wide margin. My son is currently. lying in the hospital. His condition is. still unclear. I do not wish to say. anything more. May God bless our. country, and bless Taiwan. At the same. time, Blue camp legislators Kuo Su-chun. and Wu Yu-sheng, at Eric Chu's campaign. event, shouted to use ballots to. sanction violence, not let Sean Lien's. blood flow in vain, and to turn the. public's grief and anger into voting. momentum. As for the Green camp, Su. Tseng-chang immediately stopped the. music at his rally, personally took the. stage to condemn the violence, and. urged his supporters to remain calm. That night, no one in Taipei slept well. ; this bullet would inevitably have a. major impact on the election, but which. side would it tip the race toward? No. one knew, and so, the election arrived. on the voting day of November 27th. Under the impact of the Sean Lien. shooting, the voter turnout in Taipei. City once again surged to over seventy. percent, reaching 70.65%. After the. vote counting began at 4 PM, Lung-bin. led from the very start, and the gap.

never narrowed. By shortly after 7 PM,. Lung-bin surpassed 700,000 votes and. declared victory at his campaign. headquarters. In the final count,. Lung-bin took 790,000 votes, a vote. share of about 56%, while Su. Tseng-chang took 620,000 votes, about. 44%; the gap was 160,000 votes, nearly. 12 percentage points. Of the 12. administrative districts, Lung-bin won. 10, while Su Tseng-chang only won. Shilin and Datong Districts, the. traditional Green camp strongholds. Hau. Lung-bin was not only re-elected, but. he also received 100,000 more votes. than in 2006. As for Su Tseng-chang,. the gap between him and Hau Lung-bin. was larger than expected; he shed tears. and bowed at the concession rally,. saying he was sorry to the voters who. supported him. Although supporters in. the audience chanted "Run for President. ," Su Tseng-chang did not respond to it. . Looking at the five major cities, the. KMT won Taipei and New Taipei, narrowly. held onto Taichung, while the DPP took. Tainan and Kaohsiung; the final result. was 3-2. The KMT had no advantage in. the total vote count, while the DPP. failed to flip the seat count, a result. that both sides were dissatisfied with. Looking back at the 2010 Taipei mayoral. election, the controversy stemming from. that bullet did not end with the. election. Some Green camp supporters. remained skeptical about the. authenticity of the Sean Lien shooting,. and even expressed doubts that he could. recover so quickly from such a serious. gunshot wound. However, at that time,. Ko Wen-je, then head of the Trauma. Division at NTU Hospital, who assembled. the team of physicians, stepped forward. to testify and used his deep-green. political stance to endorse the fact. that Sean Lien’s gunshot wound was. genuine. But I believe these parties. involved certainly never expected that. this public statement by Ko Wen-je. would, four years later, become a. lethal blow impacting the 2014 Taipei. mayoral election debate stage. As for. how many votes that bullet actually. swayed? The KMT's internal assessment. later estimated that the shooting. incident drove voter turnout up by four. to five percentage points; the Hao camp. initially estimated a lead of only. 50,000 votes, but ended up winning by. 170,000. However, if you lay out the. polling for the entire year, the truth. is that after the opening of the Flora. Expo, Hau Lung-bin had already returned. to the lead in most polls; that bullet. widened the margin, but did not change. the outcome. The court ultimately. determined that the shooter, Lin. Cheng-wei, actually had a financial. dispute with Chen Hung-yuan's father,. and the intended target was Chen; but. due to poor eyesight, he mistook the. person and hit Sean Lien. The life. sentence was finalized in 2013. Beyond. the shooting incident, this election. also left behind several other. memorable points. One of them was how. Su Tseng-chang’s team ushered in a. new political aesthetic; the slogan " Taipei Beyond Taipei," while criticized. by some as empty, had a quality in its. overall campaign material that truly. appealed to Taipei citizens. This. strategy became a model for many DPP. politicians later on; whether it’s Ko. Wen-je, whom the DPP helped in the 2014. election, or even Shen Pao-yang this. year in 2026, you can see the shadow of. Su Tseng-chang in their campaign. propaganda styles. Finally, worth. mentioning is Hau Lung-bin’s crisis. management; although the first half was. a bit slow, the major staff reshuffle. in the second half effectively stopped. the bleeding. Yet, what truly saved Hau. Lung-bin was the positive reception of. the Flora Expo in Taipei, which brought. his campaign back to life and widened. the gap between him and Su Tseng-chang. It was an election where the lead. swapped back and forth several times,. only to ultimately freeze on a bullet. that hit the wrong person. What about.

you? Did you visit the Flora Expo in. 2010? What other memorable moments from. this election do you have? Feel free to. leave a comment below to help complete. the story. This is He.

值得閱讀的理由

  • 從永和槍擊案切入，呈現一場突發暴力事件如何震撼選舉現場，並牽動全台政治氣氛。
  • 梳理馬英九政府上任後的經濟與災害應對考驗，說明藍綠勢力如何在選前消長。
  • 解析五都改制、候選人布局與政治人物的總統大位考量，帶出選戰背後的策略角力。
  • 回顧郝龍斌市政爭議與蘇貞昌、蔡英文的選擇，理解2010年台北市長選戰的形成脈絡。

摘要

永和槍響：選前夜的震撼

2010年11月26日，五都選舉前夕，台北縣永和市的造勢活動傳出槍聲。站在台上為議員候選人陳鴻源助選的連勝文臉部中彈，子彈也波及一名民眾，對方不幸身亡。連勝文緊急送醫，經台大醫院醫療團隊搶救後脫離險境，並逐漸康復。檢方調查認定，槍手原本意圖刺殺陳鴻源，因兩人臨時更換位置，連勝文才意外成為目標。槍擊讓選舉造勢瞬間轉為悲憤，也使台灣社會再度陷入政治暴力與未知恐慌的陰影。

政局轉折與五都改制

作者將時間帶回2008年，馬英九以高票當選總統，國民黨也在立法院占有優勢，藍營一度氣勢如虹。然而，金融海嘯重創經濟，股市大幅下跌；2009年莫拉克風災後，政府的救災表現又遭到批評，馬政府聲望下滑。民進黨則在蔡英文帶領下，逐步走出2008年敗選低潮，並在地方選舉與立委補選中回升。

2010年，台灣進行五都改制，台北縣升格為新北市，台中、台南與高雄則改制或合併為直轄市，地方選舉也因此延後舉行。改制帶來行政資源與席次變化，也引發各種政治揣測，並加劇民進黨內部的提名競爭。無論改制背後是否另有盤算，民進黨的重要人物都必須投入五都選戰。

台北市的市政挑戰與選戰布局

國民黨已在台北市執政多年，但郝龍斌第一任期面臨不少市政風波。貓空纜車因颱風造成塔柱地基問題而停駛一年半；內湖線通車後故障頻繁，甚至發生乘客受困高架軌道的狀況，遭網友譏稱「爆炸彎」。這些事件使郝龍斌支持度跌落，也讓民進黨看見重奪台北市的機會。

民進黨原先盤算由蔡英文角逐台北市長、蘇貞昌參選新北市長，認為這樣較有勝算。但蘇貞昌與蔡英文都被視為2012年總統大選的潛在人選，參選五都時也面臨政治進退的盤算：若當選市長，日後角逐總統可能被視為離職另謀高就；若在台北敗選，則有機會轉而投入總統選戰。

蘇貞昌改變布局，北台灣對決成形

2010年3月，蘇貞昌在保安宮前宣布參選台北市長，並承諾若當選便做滿任期、不考慮參選2012年總統。他還以美國總統華盛頓為例，強調民主政治應抵抗權力誘惑。蘇的宣布打亂黨中央原先的安排，蔡英文隨後轉而投入新北市長選戰。於是，台北市形成郝龍斌對決蘇貞昌的局面，新北市則由蔡英文迎戰朱立倫，北台灣兩座城市成為全台選戰焦點。

從年初的市政爭議到選前夜的致命槍響，2010年的台北市長選戰籠罩在政治競逐與社會不安之中。永和槍擊案不只改變了造勢現場的氣氛，也使這場五都選舉增添難以預料的陰影；作者由此展開對歷屆台北市長選舉的回顧。

================================================

November 26, 2010, was a mild Friday. evening. Politicians were on stage. passionately canvassing for votes,. while the crowds below were cheering. and shouting. It was the eve of the. 2010 five-city mayoral elections. At. 8:17 PM, a gunshot rang out in Yonghe. City, Taipei County, followed by the. screams of the crowd, adding suspense. and terror to an already restless night. . Lien Sheng-wen, son of Lien Chan, who. was on stage supporting council. candidate Chen Hung-yuan, suddenly. covered his face in blood. He had been. shot; the bullet had passed through his. face. An ambulance rushed him to the. nearby Cardinal Tien Hospital, before. he was transferred to National Taiwan. University Hospital. NTU Hospital. Superintendent Chen Ming-fong urgently. appointed Ko Wen-je, director of the. Trauma Department, to assemble a. medical team to save Lien Sheng-wen. In. Taipei at the same time, upon hearing. the news that Lien Sheng-wen had been. shot, the boisterous rallies, booming. music, and rhythmic campaign slogans. all came to a sudden halt. The crowd,. previously jubilant, suddenly turned. somber. It felt like a storm was. brewing, and the atmosphere grew tense. with indignation. Sheng-wen's father,. Lien Chan, took the stage in tears, and. KMT legislator Wu Yu-sheng led the. crowd in shouting, "Do not let. Sheng-wen's blood be shed in vain!" The. bullet, after passing through Lien. Sheng-wen’s face, also struck a. bystander, who unfortunately did not. survive. Lien Sheng-wen was eventually. stabilized after treatment at NTU. Hospital and went on to make a full. recovery. As for the shooter, after. thorough investigation by the. prosecution, it was determined to be a. case of mistaken identity. The shooter. had originally intended to target the. event's protagonist, Councilor Chen. Hung-yuan. Unexpectedly, Chen and Lien. had swapped positions, allowing Chen to. escape and leaving Lien to take the. bullet instead. However, this stray. bullet changed the fate of the. five-city elections and once again. plunged Taiwan's democracy into the. same panic brought by the unknown seen. in the 2004 presidential election. In. this year's "Campaign Storytelling" series, we will review every Taipei. mayoral election starting from 1994. Today, we start with the gunshot in. Yonghe, as we look back at 2010—a. year that began with vegetable politics. and ended with a bullet. Year. Hello,. this is Little Niu. Welcome to "Little. Niu Talks Politics." To talk about the. 2010 Taipei mayoral election, we must. first board a time machine and return. to 2008, when Ma Ying-jeou began his. presidency. In March 2008, Ma Ying-jeou. was elected president with a landslide. of 7.65 million votes. The KMT held. more than two-thirds of the seats in. the Legislative Yuan, successfully. completing the second transition of. power. The Blue camp's momentum was. truly unstoppable. But the Ma. administration's honeymoon period. didn't last long. In the second half of. 2008, the global financial crisis hit,. and Taiwan's economy didn't get better. immediately, as the KMT had promised. The stock market index also plunged,. dropping from a high of 9,859 points in. 2007 to a low of 3,955 points in 2008,. a staggering 57%decline. In 2009,. Typhoon Morakot struck, and the Ma. administration was heavily criticized. for its disaster response, causing. approval ratings to plummet. Meanwhile,. after a crushing defeat in the 2008. presidential election, Tsai Ing-wen. took over as DPP chair amidst a state. of disarray. Through one election after. another, she led the DPP to slowly. climb out of the 2008 trough. Vote. shares saw a significant rebound in the. 2009 local elections, where they even. reclaimed Yilan County, followed by. further victories in legislative. by-elections. By 2010, Taiwan underwent. a major administrative restructuring,.

known as the "Five Cities" reform. Taipei County was upgraded to New. Taipei City, while Taichung, Tainan,. and Kaohsiung merged their county and. city governments. Taiwan went from. having two special municipalities to. five, which together account for about. 60%of the island's population. This. upgrade had a side effect: local. elections originally scheduled for late. 2009 were postponed to late 2010 to. coincide with the Taipei and Kaohsiung. mayoral races. This sparked numerous. conspiracy theories, such as how the. number of southern administrative seats. was halved because Tainan and Kaohsiung. counties were merged with their. respective cities. Beyond reducing. seats, the upgrade also forced internal. conflict within the DPP. For example,. Chen Chu and Yang Chiu-hsing had a. falling out over the nomination for the. 2010 Kaohsiung mayoral election. Another theory suggests the upgrade. delayed the New Taipei election by a. year, giving the struggling incumbent,. Chou Hsi-wei, breathing room and. allowing Eric Chu, waiting in the wings. , a full year to prepare his campaign. Once Eric Chu played his card, the DPP. had to field their strongest candidate. at the time, former Magistrate Su. Tseng-chang, if they wanted to win New. Taipei City. If Su Tseng-chang ran for. mayor of New Taipei, he couldn't afford. to lose, but if he won, he would be. tied to the city, unable to immediately. run for president. These claims, of. course, are just hearsay. After all,. for many local city and county leaders,. upgrading to a special municipality. naturally means more funding. Though. people questioned the motives behind. the Ma Ying-jeou administration’s. upgrade plan, when it was actually time. to implement it, no one opposed it. The. actual result was that the DPP's top. figures were all forced to enter the. 2010 five-city mayoral elections. At. the time, the two most prominent. presidential-level figures in the. Pan-Green camp, Su Tseng-chang and Tsai. Ing-wen, were naturally tasked with the. two cities—Taipei and New Taipei. For. the Pan-Blue camp, since Ma Ying-jeou. handed over the baton to Hau Lung-bin,. they had been in power in Taipei for 12. consecutive years. Was this seemingly. impregnable fortress still secure at. that time? On the surface, the Pan-Blue. base was still very stable, but there. were quite a few cracks appearing. inside. During Hau Lung-bin's first. term, a number of issues emerged in the. city's governance. In September 2008,. Typhoon Sinlaku struck, hollowing out. the foundation of the Maokong Gondola's. towers, which kept the gondola shut. down for a year and a half. In July. 2009, the MRT Neihu Line opened, but it. broke down constantly, even leaving. passengers trapped on elevated tracks. to walk back along the line. The line,. then known as the Muzha-Neihu Line, was. even sarcastically dubbed the " Explosive Arc Line" by netizens. Hau. Lung-bin’s approval rating plummeted. to rock bottom, suddenly giving the DPP. a glimmer of hope for the election. This was quite possibly the DPP’s. best chance to retake the capital since. losing power in Taipei in 1998. The. question arose: who should they send to. run? As mentioned earlier, after the. major defeat in 2008, the DPP had two. trump cards on the table: Su. Tseng-chang and Tsai Ing-wen. The. DPP’s original plan was to have the. fresh and moderate-looking Tsai Ing-wen. run for Taipei mayor, while Su. Tseng-chang would run for the first New. Taipei mayor in the city where he had. served as county magistrate for eight. years. This combination seemed to offer. the highest win rate. However, the word. "win" was exactly where the problem lay. . Su Tseng-chang and Tsai Ing-wen were. both heavy hitters preparing to aim for. the 2012 presidential election. For. them, there was only one scenario for. 2010: a noble defeat. Only after a. defeat could they smoothly move on to.

the presidential race. The template was. Chen Shui-bian, who after losing in. 1998, went on to win the 2000. presidential election and successfully. took the presidency. That’s right,. only a noble defeat would provide that. opportunity. If they won the 2010. five-city election, running for. president in 2012 would be seen as " deserting" their post. As for which. special municipality to run in to have. the possibility of a noble defeat? The. answer is clear: it’s the capital. city, Taipei. While Tsai Ing-wen had. yet to clearly state her intention to. run for mayor, Su Tseng-chang, in March. 2010, caught everyone off guard by. holding a press conference in front of. the Dalongdong Baoan Temple to. officially announce his candidacy for. the 2010 Taipei mayoral election. Su. even swore before the gods that if. elected mayor of Taipei, he would serve. his full term and would not consider. the 2012 presidential election. He even. brought up George Washington, saying. that while Washington could have run. for a third term, he chose not to,. resisting temptation and setting a. precedent, which he called the essence. of democracy. Su dared not go against. that, implying he would absolutely. never return to New Taipei City to run. for a third time. Ha, well, as for why. he eventually went back to run for. mayor of New Taipei City for a third. time in 2018, that is another story. entirely. Su Tseng-chang’s proactive. move disrupted the party center's plan. to have Tsai attack Taipei while Su. defended New Taipei. Although Tsai was. the party chair, her response was very. polite, directly affirming Su's. willingness to take on the heavy. responsibility, but this also meant her. only next step was to run for mayor of. New Taipei City. Just like that, with. the party heavyweights finding their. battlegrounds, the 2010 Taipei mayoral. election was set to be between the. incumbent KMT candidate Hau Lung-bin. and the DPP's Su Tseng-chang, while the. newly upgraded New Taipei City featured. a marquee showdown between Tsai Ing-wen. and Eric Chu. The two northern cities. immediately became the hottest. battlegrounds in all of Taiwan. Wait,. let's pause the story right here for a. moment. If you enjoy the content of. this episode, please help us by hitting. that subscribe button. Subscribing is. easy for you, and it won't affect your. YouTube homepage algorithm at all, but. for us, the subscription count is the. most meaningful encouragement. One. person subscribes, one person is happy; 200,000 subscribers, 200,000 people. happy; let's grow together. As for the. public reaction? In the days. surrounding Su’s announcement, a. United Daily News poll showed Hau. Lung-bin at 46%and Su Tseng-chang at 37. %, with the Blue camp leading by nine. percentage points. However, at the same. time, a TVBS poll had Su Tseng-chang at. 44%, overtaking Hau Lung-bin’s 42%. This race looked competitive, and the. gap between the two was indeed the. smallest it had been since 1998. However, Su Tseng-chang was very clear. about one thing: the DPP's ceiling in. Taipei City has historically been stuck. around 40%, and he couldn't win using. the traditional Blue vs. Green. confrontational strategy. So, Su's. campaign made a decision that shocked. the political scene at the time: they. completely de-politicized their image,. treating their campaign propaganda like. a personal brand. Su Tseng-chang’s. campaign theme was "Taipei Beyond. Taipei," minimizing the high-saturation. , high-brightness greens often seen in. Green camp events and adding bright. pink and orange to the main visual. design. While past campaigns would. release one or two theme songs, Su’s. team produced a full urban concept. album, "Open Taipei," featuring 11. tracks, 20 creative teams, and 33. musicians, with songs in Mandarin,. Taiwanese, Hakka, English, and even.

Vietnamese. Because many singers were. tied to management contracts, they had. to appear under pseudonyms, such as " Shui Xi Gong." Fire EX. became "P-Li. Bird No. 4," Suming became "San Yin," and PTT music critics even called it. one of the best Mandarin albums of 2010. . Su’s campaign headquarters was. named the "Beyond Shop," a concept. store selling cultural goods, hosting. lectures, and playing music; young. people could drink coffee inside and. take home campaign merchandise at the. same time. To connect the campaign with. the rising online communities of that. time, Su hired a video team to film the. campaign staff’s daily routines,. launching an "Open Campaign" reality. show, updated weekly on YouTube. However, the stars of the videos. weren't the candidates, but Su’s. staffers. Through their perspective,. the public not only understood the. practical operations of a campaign but. also got closer to Su Tseng-chang as a. person—a first in Taiwan's election. history. This set of propaganda and. visual systems can be said to have. completely overturned election. aesthetics. To tell a story from 10. years later: in January 2021, when the. Control Yuan released its financial. disclosure report, Su Tseng-chang, then. Premier, declared a collection of items. worth zero dollars, including designs. for "Open Taipei,""Beyond Taipei," and. the "Beyond Shop." These were all from. his 2010 campaign. He clearly still. views the design of that visual system. as a priceless asset even today. As for. Hau Lung-bin, the KMT Central Committee. officially nominated him for. re-election in May. He immediately set. his campaign theme as "Taipei Fly High,. " appealing to the timing of his. governance, with KMT Secretary-General. King Pu-tsung directing the campaign,. hoping to reawaken the dense grassroots. base of the Blue camp in Taipei and. replicate the winning script of the. past few years. Throughout the first. half of the year, various polls were. neck-and-neck within the margin of. error. According to a TVBS poll in May,. Hau Lung-bin had 46%and Su Tseng-chang. had 41%. Hau led by a small margin most. of the time, but the lead never widened. enough to make the Blue camp feel. secure. It was right at this moment. that an unforeseen storm erupted,. triggered by nothing but a single stalk. . In 2010, the Taipei City Government. was busy from top to bottom preparing. for the Taipei International Flora. Exposition, or "Flora Expo" for short. Mayor Hau Lung-bin positioned the Flora. Expo as a major international event,. pouring massive funding and resources. into preparations and promotion. The. lineup of celebrity spokespersons was. incredibly luxurious, from image. ambassador Lin Chi-ling to theme song. performers like S.H.E., Jay Chou, A-Mei. , and Mayday—all were spokespeople. for the Expo. Since it was a. world-class expo, opposition city. councilors immediately grabbed their. magnifying glasses to scrutinize it. They didn't know what they would find,. but they were shocked by what they saw. This investigation uncovered the most. famous batch of vegetables in Taiwan's. electoral history. A single stalk of. water spinach planted in the Flora Expo. park was priced at 500 NTD, meaning one. stalk cost 20 NTD. Other items like. basil and bok choy—things that cost. just a few dozen dollars at the market. —all appeared on the list with. absurdly high unit prices. Think about. it: the general public might not. understand urban planning budget items,. but everyone knows what 500 NTD for. water spinach means—every mom who has. been to a wet market understands that. perfectly. This controversy immediately. escalated into a political crisis for. Hau Lung-bin. Political talk shows. discussed every night why a single. stalk of water spinach could skyrocket. to over a hundred dollars. Opposition. councilors even went directly to the.

Taipei District Prosecutors Office to. sue Hau for corruption and cronyism. As. soon as the water spinach scandal broke. , the city government punished two. officials from the Parks and Street. Lights Office and referred the. consulting firm for investigation,. emphasizing that there was no. corruption, only an issue with the. vendor's quoting and pricing units. The. Blue camp hit back, saying the. opposition was using a magnifying glass. to find faults and slapping a. corruption label on the Flora Expo. They emphasized that the Expo lasted. for six months and the plants had to be. replaced several times, so the unit. prices naturally couldn't be compared. to a wet market. However, the more the. city government tried to explain, the. worse it got! Spokesperson Chao. Hsin-ping emphasized that the. specifications for the water spinach at. the Flora Expo were different from what. people buy at the market: they were 20. centimeters by 20 centimeters. But this. explanation failed to clarify that it. was the planting area, and it. immediately became a laughingstock. People joked, "Where on earth could you. grow such thick water spinach?" Facing. the political crisis sparked by Hau. Lung-bin over the water spinach scandal. , Su Tseng-chang’s camp played it. smart, continuing to host town hall. meetings and concerts to discuss their. vision for the city. As for the polls,. the tide turned; the September 8th TVBS. poll showed Su Tseng-chang leading Hau. Lung-bin 42%to 39%. TVBS also projected. the final vote share. If the election. were held tomorrow, Su Tseng-chang. would receive 52%and Hau Lung-bin 48%. In other words, with less than three. months to go, the incumbent mayor was. trailing in major media polls, and. internal KMT rumors began to spread. that the Flora Expo would drag down the. five-city elections. Beyond that,. prosecutors began investigating the. Xinsheng Elevated Bridge renovation. project, meaning Hau Lung-bin was. facing not just a propaganda war, but. an administrative one. On the evening. of September 13, 2010, the Taipei City. Government held an emergency press. conference where Hau Lung-bin. personally stepped in front of the. cameras to announce the resignation of. Deputy Mayor Lee Yong-ping. Mayor's. advisor Chuang Wen-szu and Mayor's. chief secretary Jen Hsiao-chi also had. their resignations approved. These. three were all core staff members of. the city government. Outsiders. interpreted it bluntly: this was a " tail-cutting to survive" tactic to. salvage a dismal campaign. Of course,. firing people wasn't enough; Hau. Lung-bin also publicly apologized to. the citizens, admitted to procurement. mismanagement, and released the entire. Flora Expo procurement list for public. scrutiny. The goal, naturally, was to. ensure the Flora Expo, set to begin. trial operations in October, could. distance itself from the cloud of. scandal. In truth, at this stage of the. battle, both Blue and Green camps had. exhausted their ammunition of scandals. and attacks. Only one thing remained to. decide the outcome: was the Flora Expo. actually any good? After all, with 9.5. billion NTD invested and the label of. an "international event," if it. accidentally became an international. laughingstock, Hau Lung-bin—who hoped. the Expo would boost his campaign—. might find his poll numbers sinking. even further. As the Flora Expo began. its trial runs in October, the four. major park areas showcased the full. integration of Taiwan’s unique floral. technology and innovation. The first. citizens to enter emerged and told. reporters, "It’s really beautiful. Waiting in line for so long was worth. it." By the time of the official. opening on November 6, the massive. crowds immediately captured media. attention. The positive publicity. quickly overshadowed the previous wave.

of negativity. Television news. headlines shifted from "500 NTD for a. head of water spinach" to "Dream. Pavilion reservation tickets sold out. in seconds." With floral displays and. fireworks, the Flora Expo transformed. from Hau Lung-pin's biggest burden into. his greatest asset for reelection. Forty days after opening, the number of. visitors surpassed two million, and. visitor satisfaction reached a high of. eighty percent; Hau Lung-pin's poll. numbers rebounded along with it. In the. final TVBS poll before the election,. Hau stood at 49%and Su Tseng-chang at. 39%, with the gap widening back to 10. percentage points. However, because Su. Tseng-chang had led in the polls for a. period, the Pan-Green camp remained. optimistic. As for the Pan-Blue side,. despite seeing polls that showed a lead. , they still wouldn't guarantee a. victory. The race remained in this. state of anxious tension. Thus. We. return to the opening night, November. 26, 2010, the eve of the five-city. elections. Hau Lung-pin held a rally on. Ketagalan Boulevard, while Su. Tseng-chang hosted a concert-style. event at the Huashan Creative Park,. hoping to keep the joyful, positive. election atmosphere going until the. very last moment. Yet, the happy. atmosphere took a sharp turn for the. worse. At 8:00 PM, over at Yonghe. Elementary School, city councilor Chen. Hung-yuan was holding his pre-election. rally, having invited Sean Lien, a. member of the KMT Central Committee, to. speak on stage. At 8:17 PM, a man in. black climbed onto the stage, grabbed. Sean Lien around the neck from behind,. pulled out a handgun, and fired a shot. at his face at close range, with the. bullet passing through his left cheek. and exiting near his right temple. Unexpectedly, one shot wasn't enough; he tried to fire a second! At that. moment, the handgun jammed, and those. on stage rushed forward to subdue him. This man was named Lin Cheng-wei, 48. years old, a local gang member from. Yonghe nicknamed "Horse Face." The. bullet that passed through Sean Lien's. face flew into the crowd below,. striking a 29-year-old man in a. wheelchair named Huang Yun-sheng. He. was rushed to Gengxin Hospital, but. attempts to save him failed. He was the. one who truly lost his life that night. As for Sean Lien, covered in blood, he. was first sent to Yonghe Gengxin. Hospital, then transferred to National. Taiwan University Hospital, where he. survived after emergency surgery. When. the news reached the Ketagalan. Boulevard rally, Hau Lung-pin's event. was underway. The crowd was instantly. incensed, especially when Sean Lien's. father, Lien Chan, stepped onto Hau's. stage. The audience and those on stage. were instantly reduced to tears, and. Lien Chan said this:. >> I support Hau Lung-bin to be elected by. a wide margin. My son is currently. lying in the hospital. His condition is. still unclear. I do not wish to say. anything more. May God bless our. country, and bless Taiwan. At the same. time, Blue camp legislators Kuo Su-chun. and Wu Yu-sheng, at Eric Chu's campaign. event, shouted to use ballots to. sanction violence, not let Sean Lien's. blood flow in vain, and to turn the. public's grief and anger into voting. momentum. As for the Green camp, Su. Tseng-chang immediately stopped the. music at his rally, personally took the. stage to condemn the violence, and. urged his supporters to remain calm. That night, no one in Taipei slept well. ; this bullet would inevitably have a. major impact on the election, but which. side would it tip the race toward? No. one knew, and so, the election arrived. on the voting day of November 27th. Under the impact of the Sean Lien. shooting, the voter turnout in Taipei. City once again surged to over seventy. percent, reaching 70.65%. After the. vote counting began at 4 PM, Lung-bin. led from the very start, and the gap.

never narrowed. By shortly after 7 PM,. Lung-bin surpassed 700,000 votes and. declared victory at his campaign. headquarters. In the final count,. Lung-bin took 790,000 votes, a vote. share of about 56%, while Su. Tseng-chang took 620,000 votes, about. 44%; the gap was 160,000 votes, nearly. 12 percentage points. Of the 12. administrative districts, Lung-bin won. 10, while Su Tseng-chang only won. Shilin and Datong Districts, the. traditional Green camp strongholds. Hau. Lung-bin was not only re-elected, but. he also received 100,000 more votes. than in 2006. As for Su Tseng-chang,. the gap between him and Hau Lung-bin. was larger than expected; he shed tears. and bowed at the concession rally,. saying he was sorry to the voters who. supported him. Although supporters in. the audience chanted "Run for President. ," Su Tseng-chang did not respond to it. . Looking at the five major cities, the. KMT won Taipei and New Taipei, narrowly. held onto Taichung, while the DPP took. Tainan and Kaohsiung; the final result. was 3-2. The KMT had no advantage in. the total vote count, while the DPP. failed to flip the seat count, a result. that both sides were dissatisfied with. Looking back at the 2010 Taipei mayoral. election, the controversy stemming from. that bullet did not end with the. election. Some Green camp supporters. remained skeptical about the. authenticity of the Sean Lien shooting,. and even expressed doubts that he could. recover so quickly from such a serious. gunshot wound. However, at that time,. Ko Wen-je, then head of the Trauma. Division at NTU Hospital, who assembled. the team of physicians, stepped forward. to testify and used his deep-green. political stance to endorse the fact. that Sean Lien’s gunshot wound was. genuine. But I believe these parties. involved certainly never expected that. this public statement by Ko Wen-je. would, four years later, become a. lethal blow impacting the 2014 Taipei. mayoral election debate stage. As for. how many votes that bullet actually. swayed? The KMT's internal assessment. later estimated that the shooting. incident drove voter turnout up by four. to five percentage points; the Hao camp. initially estimated a lead of only. 50,000 votes, but ended up winning by. 170,000. However, if you lay out the. polling for the entire year, the truth. is that after the opening of the Flora. Expo, Hau Lung-bin had already returned. to the lead in most polls; that bullet. widened the margin, but did not change. the outcome. The court ultimately. determined that the shooter, Lin. Cheng-wei, actually had a financial. dispute with Chen Hung-yuan's father,. and the intended target was Chen; but. due to poor eyesight, he mistook the. person and hit Sean Lien. The life. sentence was finalized in 2013. Beyond. the shooting incident, this election. also left behind several other. memorable points. One of them was how. Su Tseng-chang’s team ushered in a. new political aesthetic; the slogan " Taipei Beyond Taipei," while criticized. by some as empty, had a quality in its. overall campaign material that truly. appealed to Taipei citizens. This. strategy became a model for many DPP. politicians later on; whether it’s Ko. Wen-je, whom the DPP helped in the 2014. election, or even Shen Pao-yang this. year in 2026, you can see the shadow of. Su Tseng-chang in their campaign. propaganda styles. Finally, worth. mentioning is Hau Lung-bin’s crisis. management; although the first half was. a bit slow, the major staff reshuffle. in the second half effectively stopped. the bleeding. Yet, what truly saved Hau. Lung-bin was the positive reception of. the Flora Expo in Taipei, which brought. his campaign back to life and widened. the gap between him and Su Tseng-chang. It was an election where the lead. swapped back and forth several times,. only to ultimately freeze on a bullet. that hit the wrong person. What about.

you? Did you visit the Flora Expo in. 2010? What other memorable moments from. this election do you have? Feel free to. leave a comment below to help complete. the story. This is He.

  • 以幽默對話呈現作者陪伴伴侶體驗高價 Thermage FLX 的過程，從抽中療程到踏進診所都充滿戲劇性。

  • 呈現療程結束後對臉部線條的即時觀察，也提醒效果仍可能需要時間逐漸顯現。

摘要

意外得到的高價療程

摘要

意外得到的高價療程

作者與伴侶聊起射頻治療，並透露兩人將前往診所體驗 Thermage FLX。這項療程價值約新台幣八萬元，伴侶是在創作者協會的年末活動中抽中的大獎。作者打趣說，伴侶當時雖然幸運中獎，卻沒有感受到太多喜悅；診所人員則告訴他們，這是許多人都想得到的獎品。

療程前的說明與準備

診所人員解釋，施作時通常不建議使用麻醉膏，因為治療過程會同時釋放冷卻效果；若敷了麻醉膏，可能較難感受到冷卻，反而更容易覺得灼熱或疼痛。伴侶自認怕痛，甚至曾在拔智齒時哭泣，因此對接下來的療程十分緊張。施作前，診所依照臉部狀況規劃約 980 發，並說明會加強部分輪廓與下顎線，避開較凹陷或不適合加強的區域。

逐漸加強的疼痛考驗

療程開始後，診所人員說明臉部泛紅通常會在短時間內消退，緊實感則可能在約兩週至一個月後逐漸出現。伴侶從前段尚能忍受，逐漸感受到強度升高後的刺痛與灼熱，尤其下顎線等部位更加難熬。施打過程中，作者與診所人員不斷替她打氣；她一度痛得聽不清大家說話，也開玩笑抱怨作者把自己帶來受罪。

完成療程後的初步感受

療程結束後，伴侶形容疼痛像細小的針刺，部分敏感位置特別明顯，並感覺皮膚有種被往內推、貼合起來的感受。她原本擔心臉會腫，照鏡子後卻覺得下顎線似乎更清楚，雙下巴與法令紋附近也像是有所收緊。作者和伴侶都對鏡中的變化感到驚訝，但也提到這可能只是剛做完療程時的主觀感受。

回顧整段體驗，伴侶坦言施打到中後段時曾後悔來做療程，但結束後又覺得忍耐似乎值得。診所人員先前提醒，Thermage FLX 的定位偏向讓肌膚與輪廓更緊實，而非直接達到拉皮效果；較明顯的變化通常需要一段時間觀察。影片最後，作者與伴侶繼續討論高能量施打時的痛感，內容則在談到頸部特別疼痛之處時中止。

1980 年代末期台灣引進了電話交友中心，1990 年代則流行BB Call（呼叫器），年輕人利用數字諧音密碼（如 520 代表「我愛你」）傳達心意，使交友節奏逐漸加快。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入回顧2006年台灣政局關鍵轉折，剖析民進黨如何因高捷案與第一家庭弊案陷入空前危機。
  • 解析國民黨在馬英九帶領下如日中天的氣勢，以及黨內接班台北市長的激烈初選角逐背景。
  • 揭示親民黨主席宋楚瑜在大選失利後的政治困境，以及國親兩黨面臨整併與生存的權力博弈。

摘要

政治風暴的前奏：高捷弊案重創綠營執政

作者回顧2006年台北市長選舉前夕的台灣政局，指出當時選民焦點並非市政，而是圍繞在時任總統陳水扁家族的一連串弊案。這場政治風暴的引爆點始於2005年8月的高捷泰勞抗爭事件，檢方調查揭發高捷公司違法轉包外勞管理以牟取暴利，前總統府副秘書長陳哲男更涉入接受招待與關說疑雲。風暴最終迫使時任高雄市代理市長陳其邁請辭負責，引發民進黨在年底三合一選舉慘敗，而核准高捷興建的時任行政院長謝長廷也隨後引咎下台。

醜聞接連引爆：倒扁浪潮與權力下放

高捷弊案平息不久，陳水扁女婿趙建銘捲入台開內線交易案遭到收押，成為中華民國史上首位被羈押的第一家庭成員。隨後第一夫人吳淑珍的國務機要費案與SOGO禮券案接連引爆，激發了大規模的紅衫軍反貪倒扁運動。接踵而至的貪腐醜聞重創執政聲譽，陳水扁民調跌破兩成，在泛藍陣營發動三次罷免案的壓力下，陳水扁被迫宣布「權力下放」，將憲法以外的職權交由時任行政院長蘇貞昌主導，民進黨陷入泥淖。

藍營聲勢鼎盛與宋楚瑜的政治豪賭

與民進黨的低迷形成強烈對比，國民黨在時任黨主席馬英九的超高人氣帶領下士氣如虹，全力瞄準2008年重返執政，多位黨內菁英亦摩拳擦掌角逐2006年台北市長接班人。然而，在2004年總統大選以微小差距落敗的親民黨主席宋楚瑜，面臨政治光環遭馬英九大幅擠壓、黨內民代紛紛動搖的生存困境。為了避免親民黨在國會與地方基層邊緣化，宋楚瑜於2006年初表態不排除親自參選台北市長，企圖背水一戰以迫使國民黨坐上談判桌。

馬英九祭出條款反制與橘營磁吸效應

面對宋楚瑜參選帶來的變數，國民黨主席馬英九隨即發動反制，祭出「入黨四個月條款」，規定唯有入黨滿四個月者才能登記參選公職。此舉在親民黨內引發強烈的磁吸效應，有意參選台北市長的親民黨立委李慶安等人隨即宣布退黨並重返國民黨，讓原本就處於邊緣化的親民黨面臨更嚴峻的骨牌效應，為後續的泛藍內部整合與台北市長選戰埋下了戲劇性的衝突伏筆。

政治風暴的前奏：高捷弊案重創綠營執政

作者回顧2006年台北市長選舉前夕的台灣政局，指出當時選民焦點並非市政，而是圍繞在時任總統陳水扁家族的一連串弊案。這場政治風暴的引爆點始於2005年8月的高捷泰勞抗爭事件，檢方調查揭發高捷公司違法轉包外勞管理以牟取暴利，前總統府副秘書長陳哲男更涉入接受招待與關說疑雲。風暴最終迫使時任高雄市代理市長陳其邁請辭負責，引發民進黨在年底三合一選舉慘敗，而核准高捷興建的時任行政院長謝長廷也隨後引咎下台。

醜聞接連引爆：倒扁浪潮與權力下放

高捷弊案平息不久，陳水扁女婿趙建銘捲入台開內線交易案遭到收押，成為中華民國史上首位被羈押的第一家庭成員。隨後第一夫人吳淑珍的國務機要費案與SOGO禮券案接連引爆，激發了大規模的紅衫軍反貪倒扁運動。接踵而至的貪腐醜聞重創執政聲譽，陳水扁民調跌破兩成，在泛藍陣營發動三次罷免案的壓力下，陳水扁被迫宣布「權力下放」，將憲法以外的職權交由時任行政院長蘇貞昌主導，民進黨陷入泥淖。

藍營聲勢鼎盛與宋楚瑜的政治豪賭

與民進黨的低迷形成強烈對比，國民黨在時任黨主席馬英九的超高人氣帶領下士氣如虹，全力瞄準2008年重返執政，多位黨內菁英亦摩拳擦掌角逐2006年台北市長接班人。然而，在2004年總統大選以微小差距落敗的親民黨主席宋楚瑜，面臨政治光環遭馬英九大幅擠壓、黨內民代紛紛動搖的生存困境。為了避免親民黨在國會與地方基層邊緣化，宋楚瑜於2006年初表態不排除親自參選台北市長，企圖背水一戰以迫使國民黨坐上談判桌。

馬英九祭出條款反制與橘營磁吸效應

面對宋楚瑜參選帶來的變數，國民黨主席馬英九隨即發動反制，祭出「入黨四個月條款」，規定唯有入黨滿四個月者才能登記參選公職。此舉在親民黨內引發強烈的磁吸效應，有意參選台北市長的親民黨立委李慶安等人隨即宣布退黨並重返國民黨，讓原本就處於邊緣化的親民黨面臨更嚴峻的骨牌效應，為後續的泛藍內部整合與台北市長選戰埋下了戲劇性的衝突伏筆。

摘要

政治風暴的前奏：高捷弊案重創綠營執政

作者回顧2006年台北市長選舉前夕的台灣政局，指出當時選民焦點並非市政，而是圍繞在時任總統陳水扁家族的一連串弊案。這場政治風暴的引爆點始於2005年8月的高捷泰勞抗爭事件，檢方調查揭發高捷公司違法轉包外勞管理以牟取暴利，前總統府副秘書長陳哲男更涉入接受招待與關說疑雲。風暴最終迫使時任高雄市代理市長陳其邁請辭負責，引發民進黨在年底三合一選舉慘敗，而核准高捷興建的時任行政院長謝長廷也隨後引咎下台。
